question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,-2]\times [-3,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-10 \\ {y}^{3}-3x\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[-2,\,-2]^{T}.$ Round your answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{1}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
$-1.967$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-10) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-10) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}-3x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}-3x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ -3 & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ -3 & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-10 \\ {y}^{3}-3x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ -3 & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-10 \\ {y}^{3}-3x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(-2) & 2(-2) \\ -3 & 3(-2)^{2}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}-10 \\ (-2)^{3}-3(-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-4 & -4 \\ -3 & 12\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-4)\cdot 12-(-4)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}12 & 4 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{60}[\begin{aligned}-32 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{38}{15} \\ -\frac{59}{30}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-2.533 \\ -1.967\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
